newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN MACROECONOMIC PLAN "ABSTRACT" - BUTHELEZI.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN MACROECONOMIC PLAN "ABSTRACT" - BUTHELEZI.

text.p: Inkatha Freedom Party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi criticised the South African government's macroeconomic strategy on Monday as "abstract" and said there were no firm ideas on how to implement it.

President Nelson Mandela's main black political rival also called for the government to implement promised privatisation "(The strategy) does not contain implementing tactics and it may remain as much a manifesto of abstract economic intentions as the Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP) has turned out to be," Buthelezi, who is also Home Affairs Minister, told the National African Federated Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
The RDP, launched after the 1994 elections to help kick-start South Africa's economy with particular attention to the poorest sectors of society, foundered and has quietly faded from the limelight.
The macroeconomic strategy, launched in June with ambitious targets for stimulating growth and cutting spending, has superseded large parts of the RDP.
"It is legitimate to raise the question of whether the macroeconomic strategy...will create the basis on which extensive programmes of economic empowerment may take place," Buthelezi said.

"Many of the assumptions of this strategy depend on factors which are outside government control, or which require a precision in government execution which I fear is not within the parameters of present administrative and political feasibility."
"I wish South Africa could find the strength and the determination to put itself on a clear course of economic growth," Buthelezi said.
He said the government was indecisive about privatisation.
"There must be a constitutionally entrenched mandate to force government to privatise and to undertake the maximum reasonable effort in the direction of deregulation," he said.
